text: The character Talle in the story was popularly known as _____.
explanation: Talle was known in Lafayette as "The Quiet One" because of his reserved demeanor.

text: The students were told to look _______ the difficult words in the dictionary.
explanation: The phrasal verb "look up" means to search for information in a reference book.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound in *sit*.
explanation: The 'a' in village /ˈvɪl.ɪdʒ/ makes the short /ɪ/ sound, matching sit /sɪt/.

text: Instruction: Choose the word that rhymes with the given word. Choose the word that rhymes with *comb*.
explanation: Both comb and home share the sound ending /əʊm/.

text: The committee has submitted _____ report to the board.
explanation: Its is the possessive adjective modifying report, matching the singular collective noun committee.

text: You had better _______ your homework before going out.
explanation: "Had better" is followed by a bare infinitive (base form of verb without "to").

text: He is the candidate _____ credentials impressed the interview board.
explanation: Whose is the possessive relative pronoun modifying credentials.

text: The governor frowned at the _____ which slowed down policy decisions.
explanation: Bureaucracy refers to excessive administrative routine and red tape that causes delays in governance.

text: Who is the Managing Director (MD) of Stardom Schools?
explanation: Mrs. Ibidun Gloss serves as the Managing Director of the institution.

text: Who introduced the snail delicacy to the girls in the hostel?
explanation: Ngozi, who comes from the Eastern part of Nigeria, introduced snails to her roommates.

text: Critics of cash transfer schemes believe they *discourage self-reliance*.
options: Make people overly dependent on assistance
explanation: Discouraging self-reliance means fostering dependency on external aid.

text: Instruction: Choose the word that rhymes with the given word. Choose the word that rhymes with *battle*.
explanation: Battle /ˈbæt.əl/ and raffle /ˈræf.əl/ share the exact final vowel-consonant phonetic structure.

text: The government has taken steps to curb the _____ spread of the virus.
explanation: The adjective rapid appropriately modifies the noun spread.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in *Government* (/ʌ/).
explanation: "Government" and "Come" both share the short central vowel sound /ʌ/.

text: How old is Bint in the novel?
explanation: Bint is the youngest child in the family, aged 5 years old.

text: He hasn't paid the money, has he? _____, he hasn't.
explanation: In English grammar, confirming a negative statement requires a negative response (No, he hasn't).

text: The teacher insisted that every student _____ an essay before Friday.
explanation: Verbs expressing demand/insistence (insisted that...) mandate the subjunctive mood (bare infinitive write).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The minister has always *promoted* gender equality.
explanation: Promoted means advocated or supported; the opposite is opposed.

text: Birds _____ naturally flock together.
explanation: The correct idiomatic expression is "Birds of a feather flock together."

text: Not only did the speaker criticize the government, _____ he also proposed viable solutions.
explanation: The standard correlative conjunction pairing is Not only... but also.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The manager was *furious* when he discovered the accounting error.
explanation: Furious means extremely angry or enraged.

text: Musa is not only intelligent _____ also hardworking.
explanation: The correlative conjunction pairing is not only... but also.

text: Neither the principal nor the teachers _____ happy about the test results.
explanation: With neither... nor, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it (teachers, plural).

text: You had better _____ your assignment before the teacher arrives.
explanation: The expression had better is followed by the bare infinitive (verb without to).

text: By next December, my father _____ at this university for twenty years.
explanation: The future perfect tense (will have worked) is used for actions that will be completed by a specified time in the future.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The two business partners were at *daggers drawn*. This means they:
options: were very angry with each other
explanation: To be at daggers drawn means to be in extreme hostility or anger towards each other.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. My book has become *dog-eared* through use. This means that:
options: the corners of the pages are crumpled or folded
the book is shaped like a dog's ear
explanation: Dog-eared describes a book whose page corners are worn down or folded over from frequent handling.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. She decided to *put up with* her roommate's habits. This means she:
explanation: Put up with is a phrasal verb meaning to tolerate or endure without complaining.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The minister *hit the nail on the head* during the conference. This means the minister:
explanation: Hit the nail on the head means to describe or identify something precisely and accurately.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. He decided to *turn over a new leaf* after the incident. This means he:
explanation: Turn over a new leaf means to make a fresh start or change one's conduct for the better.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The project was *put on the back burner* due to budget cuts. This means the project was:
explanation: On the back burner means deferred or given reduced priority.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. They were *caught red-handed* by the security guards. This means they were caught:
options: in the act of committing the crime
explanation: Caught red-handed means caught in the middle of doing something wrong or illegal.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Bisi has become an *indispensable* member of staff.
explanation: Indispensable means absolutely necessary or essential (vital).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Mr. Brown is often described as an *astute* businessman.
explanation: Astute means showing practical wisdom, cleverness, and sharp judgment (shrewd).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. He gave a *concise* account of what happened.
explanation: Concise means expressing much in few words; short and clear (brief).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The doctor advised him to *adhere* strictly to the diet plan.
explanation: Adhere in this context means to stick to or comply with a prescribed rule/plan.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The suspect gave a *vague* response to the police.
explanation: Vague means indefinite, unclear, or obscure.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The company's decision is *irrevocable*.
explanation: Irrevocable means impossible to revoke, reverse, or alter (unchangeable).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The teacher was *adept* at handling difficult students.
explanation: Adept means highly skilled or proficient.

text: However, excessive reliance on social media can lead to social _____.
explanation: Overuse of digital platforms can lead to physical/social isolation from real-life interaction.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound in *archive*.
explanation: The a in archive makes the long /ɑː/ sound, matching the a in darkness /dɑːknəs/.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. Which syllable carries the primary stress in the word *professional*?
explanation: Words ending in -sion have primary stress on the syllable preceding the suffix (pro-FES-sion-al).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. Which syllable carries the primary stress in the verb *import*?
explanation: Two-syllable verbs usually carry primary stress on the second syllable (im-PORT).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound in *think*.
explanation: Think and thumb both feature the voiceless dental fricative sound /θ/.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the option with the same vowel sound as *sit*.
explanation: The a in village /vɪlɪdʒ/ has the short /ɪ/ sound, matching sit /sɪt/.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. Choose the word with the correct stress pattern for *photograph*.
explanation: Nouns of three syllables starting with photo- stress the first syllable (PHO-to-graph).

text: Instruction: Identify the word with a silent letter. Choose the word that has the silent letter *k*.
explanation: In knight /naɪt/, the initial letter k is unpronounced (silent).

text: Education is often called the backbone of every nation because it:
options: drives technological advancement and social progress
takes a short time to finish
explanation: Education empowers individuals and provides skills required for national development and progress.

text: Identify the sentence that is grammatically correct.
options: One of the student have finished the exam.
One of the students has finished the exam.
One of the students have finish the exam.
One of student has finished the exam.
explanation: The expression One of + plural noun (students) takes a singular verb (has).

text: Choose the correct spelling.
explanation: Accommodation is spelled with double c and double m.

text: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence: "If I _____ you, I would take the offer."
explanation: Subjunctive mood for hypothetical situations uses were for all subjects (If I were you).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word opposite in meaning to *fragile*.
explanation: Fragile means easily broken; its direct opposite is sturdy or durable.

text: What question did Bint ask her French teacher in class?
options: How to say that's very good
How to say what is your name
explanation: Bint outsmarted her French teacher by asking him how to say "you're welcome" in French.

text: What was Omar's score in his JAMB examination?
explanation: Omar scored 260 in his JAMB exam, which excited the entire family and earned him admission to study Law.

text: What is the full meaning of the acronym "IPO" as used in the novel?
explanation: IPO stands for Investigating Police Officer during the investigation of Talle's involvement in kidnapping.

text: What was Salim addicted to on his smartphone?
explanation: Salim was heavily addicted to social media platforms, which nearly got him into trouble with a fraudster/car-jacker.

text: What full meaning does EMAL stand for in the university setting?
explanation: EMAL is the shorthand code used on campus for Examination Malpractice.

text: What time does Ummi's husband usually close from work?
explanation: Ummi mentioned that her husband usually returns home from work around 6 p.m.

text: I trust John; he will _____ very well for the competition.
explanation: Modal auxiliary verbs like will are followed by the base form of the verb (prepare).

text: We _____ see him again after the incident that happened in January.
explanation: Simple past tense (didn't) is required to match the past time frame specified ("happened in January").

text: The dog belongs to the man _____ lives on the third street.
explanation: The relative pronoun who is used to refer to a person (the man).

text: The _____ of the former president have been laid to rest.
explanation: Remains (plural noun) refers specifically to a deceased person's body.

text: It is high time we _____ for the meeting.
explanation: The subjunctive phrase It is high time... is followed by a verb in the simple past tense (left).

text: Experts advise users to maintain a _____ approach.
explanation: A balanced approach is recommended to avoid negative consequences.

text: His explanation for being absent was _____ here _____ there.
explanation: Neither... nor is the correct correlative conjunction pairing.

text: He came in only when the lecturer was _____ the lecture.
explanation: Rounding off means concluding or finishing an activity/speech, whereas rounding up means gathering people or animals together.

text: The chairman and the chief executive officer _____ very hard-working.
explanation: Since "The" is used only once before "chairman", both titles refer to one single person, taking a singular verb (is).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The relationship between the boy and the girl is purely *platonic*.
explanation: Platonic means friendly and affectionate without sexual involvement; its opposite is sexual.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The principal was *elated* by the performance of his team at the competition.
explanation: Elated means extremely happy or overjoyed; the direct opposite is saddened.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. He remains a major *liability* to the community as a whole.
explanation: A liability is a handicap or disadvantage; its opposite is an asset.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The people treat their leaders with *contempt*.
explanation: Contempt means disrespect or disdain; its opposite is respect.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Drug abuse among teenagers has become a *frightening* issue in society.
explanation: Frightening in this context implies alarming or worrisome.

text: What nickname was given to Samuel Johnson in the novel?
explanation: In the novel, Samuel Johnson was affectionately called "Samjohn."

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Patients must strictly follow the doctor's *prescription*.
explanation: A medical prescription provides official medical instructions or directions for treatment.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The *indiscriminate* dumping of refuse degrades the environment.
explanation: Indiscriminate means unselective, random, or careless.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Prices of basic goods have increased at an *astronomical* rate.
explanation: Astronomical means extremely high or alarming.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Without proper interventions, the economy is *sliding deeper into a worst situation*.
explanation: Deterioration refers to the process of becoming progressively worse.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The Armed Forces had the *upper hand* in their clash with the terrorists.
options: Their hands were up during the clash
They fought the terrorists with their bare hands
They maximized the force of hand
explanation: To have the upper hand means to gain control, advantage, or dominance over someone.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The marriage *hit the rocks* barely five months after it was contracted.
options: They had an accident on the rocks
Their marriage came to an end
explanation: To hit the rocks means to fail, break down, or come to an end.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The new policy was met with cold shoulders by the staff.
options: The staff fell ill from cold weather
The staff rejected or ignored the policy
The staff welcomed the policy warmly
explanation: Giving a cold shoulder means showing intentional coldness, rejection, or indifference.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. Tunde decided to spill the beans during the police interview.
options: Tunde made a mess of the office
explanation: To spill the beans means to reveal secret or confidential information.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. She achieved her goal against all odds.
explanation: Against all odds means succeeding in spite of strong opposition or hardship.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound in *cup*.
explanation: Both cup /kʌp/ and bus /bʌs/ contain the short /ʌ/ vowel sound.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound in *feet*.
explanation: Both feet /fiːt/ and seat /siːt/ share the long /iː/ vowel sound.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound in *church*.
explanation: Church and cheap both feature the voiceless affricate /tʃ/.

text: Instruction: Identify the word with a silent letter. Choose the word with a silent letter.
explanation: In comb /koʊm/, the final 'b' is silent.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. Which syllable carries the primary stress in the word *information*?
explanation: Words ending in -tion take primary stress on the penultimate syllable (in-for-MA-tion).

text: Neither of the two candidates _____ qualified for the job.
explanation: Neither used as a pronoun takes a singular verb (is).

text: I look forward to _____ from you soon.
explanation: The phrasal verb look forward to is followed by a gerund (-ing verb form).

text: The dog wagged _____ tail happily.
explanation: Its is the possessive pronoun, whereas it's is the contraction for it is.

text: He preferred swimming _____ running.
explanation: The verb prefer takes the preposition to (prefer X to Y).

text: She has been sleeping _____ five hours.
explanation: For is used with a duration/period of time (five hours), whereas since is used with a specific starting point.

text: If I had known, I _____ gone there.
explanation: Third conditional structure: If + past perfect..., would/wouldn't have + past participle.

text: The driver was charged _____ reckless driving.
explanation: The verb charge in legal contexts collocates with the preposition with (charged with).

text: Choose the correctly spelled word.
explanation: Embarrassment is correctly spelled with double 'r' and double 's'.

text: What did Salim refer to his online date/girlfriend as before meeting her?
explanation: Salim referred to the girl he met online as his "Indian Princess" due to her social media profile.

text: Who was Tomiwa's blind date arranged with?
explanation: Tomiwa went on a blind date with Habib, a politician who was interested in her.

text: What was Omar's exact score in his JAMB examination?
explanation: Omar scored 260 in his JAMB exam, securing his admission to study Law.

text: Why was Talle arrested by the police in Lafayette?
options: Stealing money from the local market
explanation: Talle was arrested after a kidnapped boy was harbored at his house by criminals who took advantage of his quiet nature.

text: Some smugglers created a road diversion in order to _____ the new import duty.
explanation: Circumvent means to find a way around or evade a rule or duty.

text: It happened that our dog is male, but _____ are all females.
explanation: The possessive pronoun theirs does not take an apostrophe.

text: We can use the telephone; the lines are all _____.
explanation: When telephone lines are working and operational, they are said to be "up."

text: Ayayi cashed _____ our boy's defensive error to score the equalizer.
explanation: To cash in on something means to take advantage of an opportunity or mistake.

text: I heard that Italy's victory at the World Cup was announced _____ the radio.
explanation: Media broadcasts on radio, television, or the internet take the preposition on.

text: A modern car runs _____ petrol.
explanation: Vehicles or engines that consume fuel are said to run on fuel.

text: We were all delighted when the lady _____ a bouncing baby boy.
explanation: Idiomatically and formally, a woman is delivered of a child.

text: Although the problem was simple, _____ students were able to solve it.
explanation: Few has a negative connotation meaning "almost none," contrasting with "Although the problem was simple."

text: Some students have believed _____ that they can succeed without hard work.
explanation: The correct idiomatic phrase is many a time (followed by a singular noun/verb structure).

text: We watched the woman as she stood up and _____ herself more comfortably.
explanation: The simple past tense of reseat in reflexive form matching past parallel verbs (stood up) is resat.

text: The students _____ the principal's appeal for calm and took to the streets.
explanation: Defied means openly resisted or refused to obey.

text: The loud noise from the record seller's workshop _____ on my ears.
explanation: To jar on one's ears means to have an unpleasant, grating effect on hearing.

text: There's _____ ventilation in this room; that's why you can't breathe well.
explanation: Little is used with uncountable nouns (ventilation) to express an insufficient amount.

text: Whenever he turns the light on, someone _____ to disturb him.
explanation: Present habitual actions (Whenever he turns...) require the simple present tense (comes).

text: It _____ be taken for repair after all; it is working again.
explanation: Needn't expresses lack of necessity ("it is not necessary to take it for repair").

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. In the match, the underdog team turned out to be the *dark horse*.
explanation: A dark horse is a competitor who achieves unexpected success.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. He spoke with his *heart in his mouth*.
explanation: Having one's heart in one's mouth means feeling extremely nervous, frightened, or anxious.

text: The leader in today's issue of the newspaper focuses on economic inflation.
explanation: A "leader" or "leading article" in newspaper terminology refers to the editorial.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. All his elaborate plans *fell through*.
explanation: Fall through is an idiom meaning to fail or not come to fruition.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. His summary of the lecture was brief and *to the point*.
explanation: To the point means direct, relevant, and concise (precise).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The Military Governor *upheld* the decision of his cabinet.
explanation: Uphold means to confirm or maintain; its direct opposite is reverse or overturn.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Chidi is naturally *taciturn*.
explanation: Taciturn means quiet and reserved in speech; its opposite is garrulous (talkative/loquacious).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. James takes his studies rather *lightly*.
explanation: Taking something lightly means treating it without gravity; the opposite is seriously.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The woman was accused of trying to *obscure* the issue so that the public would be confused.
explanation: Obscure means to hide or make unclear; its antonym is highlight or clarify.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Do you have the same *aversion* as I do for home movies?
explanation: Aversion means strong dislike or disinclination; its opposite is liking or fondness.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. I did not think she could be so easily *taken in* by his pretenses.
explanation: To be taken in means to be fooled or deceived.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The witness was guilty of swearing to a statement he knew to be false, committing *perjury*.
explanation: Perjury specifically refers to the act of lying under oath in court.

text: The guest speaker took us down memory *lane* with her interesting stories.
explanation: Memory lane is an established idiom meaning to recall past experiences.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Her efforts produced a *consistent* improvement in her academic performances.
explanation: Consistent means regular and dependable, synonymous with steady.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The manager made an *arbitrary* decision that angered the workers.
explanation: Arbitrary means based on random choice or personal whim (caprice) rather than reason.

text: Instruction: Choose the question that the emphatic stress in the sentence answers. Sentence: I bought my *WIFE* a red dress.
options: Did I buy my husband a red dress?
Did I buy my wife a red shoe?
Did he buy my wife a red dress?
Did I buy my wife a black dress?
explanation: Capitalizing WIFE emphasizes the person who received the dress, contradicting "husband."

text: Instruction: Choose the question that the emphatic stress in the sentence answers. Sentence: Daddy plays *TENNIS* on Saturday afternoons.
options: Does mummy play tennis on Saturday afternoons?
Does daddy play tennis on Sunday afternoons?
Does daddy play tennis on Saturday morning?
Does daddy play cricket on Saturday afternoons?
explanation: Emphatic stress on TENNIS responds directly to a question asking if he plays a different sport (cricket).

text: Instruction: Choose the question that the emphatic stress in the sentence answers. Sentence: *SHE* returned from London yesterday.
options: Did she return from London today?
Did he return from London yesterday?
Did she travel to London yesterday?
Did she return from Paris yesterday?
explanation: Stressing SHE highlights the subject's identity in contrast to "he."

text: Instruction: Choose the word that rhymes with the given word. Choose the word that rhymes with *battle*.
explanation: Battle /ˈbæt.əl/ and raffle /ˈræf.əl/ share the exact final vowel and consonant syllabic sound pattern.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined letter(s) in *wash*.
explanation: Both wash /wɒʃ/ and nation /ˈneɪ.ʃən/ contain the voiceless postalveolar fricative sound /ʃ/.

text: Instruction: Choose the word with a different stress pattern among the options.
explanation: Enter /ˈen.tər/ is stressed on the first syllable, whereas develop, compare, and report are stressed on the second.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as *thin*.
explanation: Both thin /θɪn/ and theme /θiːm/ feature the voiceless dental fricative /θ/.

text: Instruction: Identify the word with a silent letter. Choose the word with a silent letter.
explanation: In debt /det/, the letter 'b' is unpronounced (silent).

text: Neither the teacher nor the students _____ present at the auditorium.
explanation: Proximity rule for neither... nor: the verb agrees with the closest subject (students, plural).

text: By this time next month, we _____ our final examinations.
explanation: Future perfect tense (will have finished) denotes an action that will be completed prior to a specific future point.

text: I would rather you _____ home now.
explanation: Would rather + subject takes a past tense verb (went) to express present subjunctive meaning.

text: Choose the correctly spelled word.
explanation: Privilege is correctly spelled without a 'd' and with two 'i's and two 'e's.

text: If I had worked harder, I _____ the test easily.
explanation: Third conditional: If + past perfect..., would have + past participle.

text: From Ummi's narration, what exactly is the "Note of Salvation"?
options: The cheat notes that Tomiwa gave Salma
The cheat notes passed to Salma in the examination hall
The official apology letter written by Salma to the HOD
The pass slip used by Omar to enter the university campus
explanation: The cheat note passed to Salma by Kolawole Abdul during the examination was nicknamed the "Note of Salvation" because she believed it would save her from failing.

text: Which of the following crimes was Talle NOT guilty of?
explanation: Talle was arrested for being complicit in a kidnapping scheme and extortion with Zaki, but he was not involved in armed robbery.

text: What was Habib's official position in politics?
explanation: In the novel, Habib was a wealthy politician holding the office of a Senator.

text: How much money did Dr. Kabir stake at the gambling joint?
explanation: Dr. Kabir staked ₦100,000 at the local gambling den hoping to double his money.

text: Which of the following was NOT one of Salma's room-mates in the university hostel?
explanation: Salma's three room-mates were Tomiwa, Ngozi, and Ada. Natasha was a contact involved with Salim on social media.

text: Cosmas is a very good friend on _____ I can rely.
explanation: The preposition on takes the objective relative pronoun whom when referring to a person (on whom I can rely).

text: A hotel is supposed to be a home away from home, but the one we _____ was hell.
explanation: The standard phrasal verb for registering one's arrival at a hotel is check into.

text: I ought _____ the letter by now.
explanation: Ought to + perfect infinitive (to have sent) expresses an unfulfilled expectation in past time relative to now.

text: Ade's fever was so acute that she _____ an injection.
explanation: Past necessity is expressed using had to followed by the base verb have (had to have).

text: By 11.00 am, I _____ writing this exam for two hours.
explanation: Future perfect continuous tense (will have been writing) is used for an ongoing action evaluated at a specified future moment (By 11.00 am).

text: The car couldn't keep pace _____ the motorcycle in congested areas.
explanation: The correct prepositional idiom is keep pace with someone or something.

text: Idris couldn't have said a thing like that, _____?
explanation: A negative sentence with the modal couldn't requires a positive question tag with the same modal (could he?).

text: They are always fighting _____.
explanation: Reciprocal pronoun one another is used for reciprocal action among more than two individuals or generic plural subjects.

text: The building _____ because of a weak structural foundation.
explanation: Buildings collapse when structural integrity fails completely.

text: Please let me have _____ salt in my soup.
explanation: Uncountable nouns like salt take a little to express a small affirmative quantity.

text: The magazine was _____ by the government for an offensive publication.
explanation: Proscribe means to officially ban or forbid something by law.

text: Many citizens reacted to the brutal murder with strong _____.
explanation: Indignation refers to righteous anger caused by something unfair or unjust.

text: The doctor _____ the illness as typhoid fever.
explanation: Medical practitioners diagnose a disease by identifying its signs and symptoms.

text: As the writer did not indicate his name, the editor published _____ article.
explanation: A piece of writing produced by an unnamed person is anonymous.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The new managing director made *prudent* investments that saved the company.
explanation: Prudent means wise and careful; its opposite is rash or reckless.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. His *frugal* lifestyle surprised many of his wealthy friends.
explanation: Frugal means thrifty or economical; the opposite is extravagant or wasteful.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The general commended the soldiers for their *valiant* effort during the war.
explanation: Valiant means brave and courageous; its antonym is cowardly.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The politician was accused of giving *ambiguous* statements to the press.
explanation: Ambiguous means vague or open to multiple interpretations; the direct opposite is clear.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. She showed a *belligerent* attitude towards her co-workers.
explanation: Belligerent means hostile or aggressive; the opposite is peaceful.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The witness gave a *meticulous* description of the robber.
explanation: Meticulous means extremely careful and precise in detail.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The government decided to *abolish* the outdated tax law.
explanation: Abolish means to officially end or nullify a law or custom.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The CEO's speech was *eloquent* and inspired everyone.
explanation: Eloquent means fluent, persuasive, and articulate in speech.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. They faced *insurmountable* difficulties during the expedition.
explanation: Insurmountable means impossible to overcome or unconquerable.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Her *altruistic* nature made her beloved in the community.
explanation: Altruistic means showing unselfish concern for the welfare of others (generous).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The manager decided to *let the cat out of the bag*.
explanation: To let the cat out of the bag means to reveal secret information, usually by mistake.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. After the argument, they decided to *bury the hatchet*.
explanation: To bury the hatchet means to end a quarrel and make peace.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The candidate was told to *pull his socks up* before the final round.
explanation: To pull your socks up means to make an effort to improve one's performance.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The news of his promotion came *out of the blue*.
explanation: Out of the blue means completely unexpected or without warning.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. I am *at my wits' end* with this technical problem.
options: Completely confused and out of ideas
explanation: To be at one's wits' end means to be so worried or confused that you don't know what to do next.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound in *archbishop*.
explanation: Archbishop /ɑːrtʃˈbɪʃ.əp/ contains the /tʃ/ sound, which matches the sound in sachet /sæˈʃeɪ/ for the consonant /ʃ/ in JAMB standard testing.

text: Instruction: Choose the word that rhymes with the given word. Choose the word that rhymes with *permit* (verb).
explanation: Permit /pəˈmɪt/ and commit /kəˈmɪt/ share the exact final stressed rhyme sound /-ɪt/.

text: Instruction: Choose the word that rhymes with the given word. Choose the word that rhymes with *boys*.
explanation: Both boys /bɔɪz/ and noise /nɔɪz/ share the diphthong ending /ɔɪz/.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. Choose the correct primary stress pattern for *productivity*.
explanation: Words ending in the suffix -ity place their primary stress on the antepenultimate syllable (producTIvity).

text: Instruction: Identify the word with a silent letter. Choose the word with a silent letter.
explanation: In doubt /daʊt/, the letter 'b' is silent.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as *sun*.
explanation: Both sun /sʌn/ and son /sʌn/ share the short /ʌ/ vowel sound.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as *them*.
explanation: Both them /ðəm/ and brother /ˈbrʌðər/ use the voiced dental fricative /ð/.

text: Scarcely had the president arrived _____ the national anthem began.
explanation: The correlative conjunction pattern Scarcely... when is mandatory in standard English.

text: He was sentenced to prison because he was found guilty _____ fraud.
explanation: The adjective guilty takes the preposition of (guilty of fraud).

text: Neither of the dresses _____ suitable for the occasion.
explanation: Pronouns like neither take a singular verb (is).

text: Choose the correctly spelled word.
explanation: Bureaucracy is the correct spelling.

text: If he had trained harder, he _____ the marathon.
explanation: Third conditional requirement: If + past perfect..., would have + past participle.

text: The police _____ investigating the cause of the fire outbreak.
explanation: In standard grammar, police is a plural noun and takes a plural verb (are).

text: Who is the principal of Stardom Schools?
explanation: Mr. Adewale Bepo is the principal of Stardom Schools, who is affectionately referred to as the "Lekki Headmaster".

text: Why was Mr. Bepo considering relocating abroad?
options: Due to family pressure and to join his wife and children in the UK
To accept a higher-paying job offer in Canada
To escape the management challenges at Stardom Schools
explanation: Mr. Bepo was torn between staying in Nigeria and fulfilling his family's wishes to join them in the United Kingdom.

text: Why was the principal nicknamed "The Lekki Headmaster"?
options: The school was located in Lekki
He humorously imitated characters from the classic TV show The Village Headmaster
He introduced a new curriculum in Lekki
explanation: His style of leadership and playful references to the legendary Nigerian television drama earned him the moniker.

text: How did the school management address the issue of student lateness?
options: Introducing interesting morning assembly activities that students didn't want to miss
Extending school hours into the evening
explanation: Stardom Schools curbed lateness by making morning assemblies engaging and value-packed rather than punitive.

text: The manager, along with his assistants, _____ expected to arrive by noon.
explanation: Phrases such as along with, together with, or as well as do not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with the main subject (The manager, singular).

text: If he _____ earlier, he would not have missed the flight.
explanation: Third conditional construction: If + past perfect (had arrived) paired with would have + past participle.

text: The principal advised that every student _____ present at the assembly.
explanation: Mandative subjunctive mood requires the bare infinitive verb (be) after verbs of advice, demand, or recommendation.

text: Each of the contestants _____ to submit their forms before Friday.
explanation: The indefinite pronoun Each is always singular and takes a singular verb (has).

text: The man was accused _____ theft by his employer.
explanation: The verb accuse correctly collocates with the preposition of.

text: He insisted _____ seeing the manager before leaving.
explanation: The verb insist takes the preposition on followed by a gerund.

text: By December this year, I _____ living in Lagos for ten years.
explanation: Future perfect continuous tense (will have been) projects the duration of an ongoing state at a specific future benchmark.

text: Neither the students nor their teacher _____ present at the hall.
explanation: Proximity rule for neither... nor: the verb agrees with the subject closest to it (teacher, singular).

text: She prefers reading novels _____ watching movies.
explanation: The verb prefer requires the preposition to (prefer X to Y).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The project requires a *rapid* response from the technical team.
explanation: Rapid is synonymous with fast, swift, or quick.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The expression "hail this as progress" means to _____ it.
explanation: To hail something means to praise or acclaim it enthusiastically.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. The company's *altruistic* donations helped rebuild the community center.
explanation: Altruistic means showing unselfish concern for others, synonymous with benevolent or generous.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. His *meticulous* research yielded flawless results.
explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail or being extremely thorough.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The market experienced an absolute *scarcity* of essential commodities.
explanation: Scarcity means a shortage or deficit; its direct antonym is abundance.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. His *frugal* spending habits allowed him to save money.
explanation: Frugal means thrifty or economical; the opposite is extravagant or wasteful.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The minister gave an *ambiguous* answer to the journalists.
explanation: Ambiguous means unclear or open to multiple interpretations; the opposite is clear.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The general praised the soldier's *valiant* conduct.
explanation: Valiant means brave; its antonym is cowardly.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. She showed a *belligerent* attitude during the discussion.
explanation: Belligerent means hostile or warlike; the opposite is peaceful or amicable.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that best explains the meaning of the underlined expression. The phrase "lungs of the city" used in urban ecology is an example of a _____.
explanation: Comparing green spaces directly to human lungs without using "like" or "as" is a metaphor.

text: To *break the cycle of poverty* means to _____.
options: Use tools like education to escape generational poverty
Prevent students from returning to school
explanation: Breaking the cycle means stopping poverty from being passed down through generations.

text: When someone is described as a *dark horse*, it implies that they _____.
explanation: A dark horse is a little-known competitor who unexpectedly triumphs.

text: To *let the cat out of the bag* means to _____.
explanation: Idiomatically, letting the cat out of the bag means revealing confidential information.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound in *cup*.
explanation: Both cup /kʌp/ and bus /bʌs/ feature the short /ʌ/ vowel sound.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound in *wash*.
explanation: Both wash /wɒʃ/ and nation /ˈneɪ.ʃən/ contain the voiceless postalveolar fricative /ʃ/.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. Which syllable carries the primary stress in *productivity*?
explanation: Words ending in the suffix -ity place primary stress on the antepenultimate syllable (pro-duc-TI-vi-ty).

text: Instruction: Identify the word with a silent letter. Choose the word with a silent letter.
explanation: In the word debt /det/, the letter 'b' is silent.

text: By this time next year, the government _____ the new expressway.
explanation: Action completed before a definite point in the future takes the future perfect tense (will have completed).

text: I would rather you _____ here with us tonight.
explanation: Would rather + subject takes the simple past tense (stayed) to express present subjunctive meaning.

text: Scarcely had the speaker stepped on the stage _____ the lights went out.
explanation: Scarcely is paired correlatively with when.

text: Neither of the options _____ acceptable to the board.
explanation: Neither as a subject pronoun takes a singular verb (is).

text: Choose the correctly spelled word.
explanation: Bureaucracy is the correct English spelling.

text: The team was rewarded because they performed _____ than expected.
explanation: Comparative degree (better) is required when comparing performance with expectations.

text: The suspect denied _____ any involvement in the fraud.
explanation: The verb deny takes a gerund object (denied having).

text: The teacher asked the students to _____ up their dictionaries.
explanation: Look up means to search for information in a reference book.

text: She has been studying _____ six hours continuously.
explanation: For is used to denote a duration or period of time (six hours).

text: If I had known earlier, I _____ you at the airport.
explanation: Conditional type 3: If + past perfect..., would have + past participle.

text: The committee members shared the money among _____.
explanation: Reflexive pronoun themselves applies when a group acts on or among its own members.

text: Hardly had I entered the house _____ it started raining.
explanation: Hardly takes the correlative conjunction when.

text: The driver was charged _____ reckless endangerment.
explanation: Legal charges take the preposition with (charged with).

text: Choose the correctly spelled word.
explanation: Embarrassment is spelled with double 'r' and double 's'.

text: What was the main reason Dr. Samuel Johnson gave Omar a hard time during registration?
explanation: JAMB novel questions frequently test candidates on administrative hurdles faced by characters during registration.

text: In literature comprehension, when a narrative begins *in media res*, where does the story start?
options: At the exact ending of events
In the middle of the action
At the birth of the protagonist
explanation: In media res is a Latin literary technique meaning "into the middle of things."

text: According to standard comprehension passages, what is considered a primary benefit of technology in education?
options: Enhancing access to information and learning resources
explanation: Passages on IT routinely highlight expanded access to educational materials.

text: Excessive use of digital devices primarily causes which health condition mentioned in passages?
explanation: Screen fatigue commonly leads to optical strain and headaches.

text: What is the author's tone when presenting both advantages and disadvantages of technology neutrally?
explanation: An unbiased presentation of both pros and cons reflects a neutral tone.

text: Which strategy best mitigates the negative effects of continuous screen time?
explanation: Time management and setting screen limits reduce digital fatigue.

text: What is the primary role of education in national development?
explanation: Education is a core tool for poverty alleviation and socio-economic development.

text: What grammatical structure is the phrase "Automation advances" when functioning as a subject?
explanation: A phrase led by a noun or noun modifier acting as a subject is a noun phrase.

text: The term "digital divide" in comprehension passages usually refers to:
options: Gap between those with and without technology access
explanation: "Digital divide" describes socio-economic inequality in access to IT.

text: In narrative structure, the turning point of highest tension in a play is called the:
explanation: The climax is the peak of action and conflict in a dramatic narrative.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Find the word nearest in meaning to *alleviate*.
explanation: Alleviate means to make suffering or a problem less severe (reduce).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Select the option nearest in meaning to *incorruptible*.
explanation: Someone who is incorruptible cannot be corrupted or bribed, meaning they are honest.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Select the word nearest in meaning to *thriving*.
explanation: To thrive means to grow or develop vigorously (flourish).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the option nearest in meaning to *deterrent*.
explanation: A deterrent is a thing that discourages or is intended to discourage an action.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word nearest in meaning to *fatal*.
explanation: Fatal means causing death (deadly).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Select the option nearest in meaning to *essential*.
explanation: Essential means absolutely necessary or vital.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Find the word nearest in meaning to *obsolete*.
explanation: Obsolete means no longer produced or used; out of date.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Select the word nearest in meaning to *ransacked*.
explanation: To ransack means to go hurriedly through a place stealing things and causing damage.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the option nearest in meaning to *robust*.
explanation: Robust means strong and healthy; vigorous.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Find the word nearest in meaning to *timely*.
explanation: Timely means done or occurring at a favorable or useful time (opportunate).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *frugal*.
explanation: Frugal means economical; its opposite is extravagant (wasteful).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *hostility*.
explanation: Hostility means unfriendliness or opposition; its antonym is friendliness.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *ephemeral*.
explanation: Ephemeral means lasting a short time; permanent means long-lasting.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *arrogant*.
explanation: Arrogant means exaggerating one's own importance; humble is the opposite.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *compulsory*.
explanation: Compulsory means required by law or rule; optional means elective.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *obscure*.
explanation: Obscure means uncertain or hard to see; clear is the direct antonym.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *abundance*.
explanation: Abundance means a large quantity; scarcity means a shortage.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *optimistic*.
explanation: Optimistic means hopeful about the future; pessimistic means expecting the worst.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *voluntary*.
explanation: Voluntary is done of one's own free will; compulsory is forced.

text: If I _______ the Managing Director, I would have promoted him immediately.
explanation: Hypothetical subjunctive mood uses "were" for all subjects ("If I were...").

text: Neither the principal nor the teachers _______ present at the meeting.
explanation: With "neither... nor", the verb agrees with the closer subject ("teachers" -> plural verb "were").

text: She has been working here _______ 2018.
explanation: "Since" is used with a specific point in time in perfect tenses.

text: Scarcely had he arrived _______ the rain started.
explanation: Correlative conjunction "Scarcely... when" is the standard grammatical pairing.

text: The committee has submitted _______ report to the board.
explanation: "Committee" is a collective noun acting as a single unit, requiring the singular possessive pronoun "its".

text: He prefers swimming _______ running.
explanation: The verb "prefer" takes the preposition "to" when making comparisons.

text: The boy is suffering _______ malaria.
explanation: The verb "suffer" takes the preposition "from" when referring to ailments.

text: Either John or his brothers _______ responsible for the damage.
explanation: In "either... or" structures, the verb agrees with the subject closer to it ("brothers" -> "are").

text: Instruction: Choose the word that has a different stress pattern from the others.
explanation: "Teacher" is stressed on the 1st syllable (TEACH-er), whereas "Prepare", "Record" (verb), and "Attend" are stressed on the 2nd syllable.

text: Instruction: Choose the word that has a different stress pattern from the others.
explanation: Two-syllable nouns are typically stressed on the 1st syllable, while "decided" is a 3-syllable word stressed on the 2nd syllable.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word with the same consonant sound as the underlined sound in *think* (/θ/).
explanation: "Think" and "Theme" both use the voiceless dental fricative /θ/, while the others use /ð/.

text: Instruction: Choose the word that rhymes with the given word. Choose the word that rhymes with *comb*.
explanation: "Comb" (/koʊm/) rhymes with "home" (/hoʊm/).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as *seat* (/iː/).
explanation: Both "seat" and "machine" contain the long vowel sound /iː/.

text: Instruction: Choose the word that contains the consonant sound /f/.
explanation: The "gh" in "tough" is pronounced as /f/.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. Choose the word that has the primary stress on the third syllable.
explanation: "Ed-u-CA-tion" has primary stress on the 3rd syllable.

text: Instruction: Identify the word with a silent letter. Choose the word with the silent letter.
explanation: The letter 'b' in "subtle" is silent.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined sound. Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as *cat* (/æ/).
explanation: "Plaid" is pronounced /plæd/, containing the same short /æ/ vowel as "cat".

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to *rigid*.
explanation: Rigid means unable to bend; flexible means easily bent or modified.

text: And avoid _____ consumption of online content.
explanation: Users are advised against excessive (uncontrolled/over-the-top) consumption.

text: Who is the narrator of the story in The Life Changer?
explanation: Ummi is the main narrator of the novel, recounting events and sharing life lessons with her children.

text: Either the boys or their father _____ going to the market.
explanation: With either... or, the verb agrees with the closer subject (father, singular).

text: The suspect denied _____ the money.
explanation: The verb deny takes a gerund object (denied stealing).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word. Her explanation was *explicit* enough for everyone to understand.
explanation: Explicit means stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for confusion.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The children await a *severe* punishment.
explanation: The opposite of severe (harsh/strict) is mild or gentle.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The tumor turned out to be *malignant*.
explanation: Malignant means harmful/cancerous; its direct opposite is benign (harmless).

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. His *apathy* towards local politics surprised his friends.
explanation: Apathy means lack of interest or concern; the opposite is enthusiasm.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The army launched a *covert* operation in the region.
explanation: Covert means secret or concealed; its opposite is open or overt.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The boy's *docile* nature made him easy to manage.
explanation: Docile means submissive/obedient; the opposite is stubborn or rebellious.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. She wore a *gaudy* outfit to the quiet ceremony.
explanation: Gaudy means extravagantly bright or showy; its opposite is simple or understated.

text: Instruction: Choose the option that is OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word. The culprit's account of the incident was *dubious*.
explanation: Dubious means hesitating, doubtful, or unreliable; the opposite is convincing or trustworthy.

text: Modern communication technology has _____ the way people interact globally.
explanation: Transformed fits the positive evolutionary change described in the context.

text: No one is there to reply, _____?
explanation: Negative indefinite pronouns like no one or nobody take a positive plural question tag (are they).

text: Distance is no longer a _____ to sharing information.
explanation: A barrier represents an obstacle, which distance no longer is due to modern technology.

text: Since the fight, Joy and Gift have refused to talk to _____.
explanation: Each other is used when referring to reciprocity between two people (Joy and Gift).

text: The plan for the party _____ due to lack of funds.
explanation: Fall through means to fail to happen or come to nothing.

text: The man as well as his children _____ present at the meeting.
explanation: When subjects are joined by as well as, the verb agrees with the first subject (The man, singular).

text: The teacher advised the students _____ late for the examination.
explanation: Reported commands/advice in the negative use the structure not + to + infinitive.

text: Hardly had the bell rung _____ the students rushed out.
explanation: The correlative conjunction pattern Hardly... when is standard in English.
